title: Githoney by TxPipe: Dev bounty system using Marlowe contracts, deep integration with Github

ms.promise:

ms.report:
Milestone Outputs:

A fee mechanism that allows to charge a small amount for each bounty processed
For the sustainability of the product we added two fees. 
First, a very small fixed feed of 2 ADA when the bounty is initiated. 
Secondly, a fee of 5% upon the successful completion of the bounty - i.e. if the bounty is not completed, and the Pull Request of the Contributor is not merged, then no fee is paid. 
A fully branded frontend describing the product and onboarding instructions

We have edited the look and feel of the documentation site so that it looks more premium and polished. The documentation site is visible here: https://docs.githoney.io/ . The documentation describes the product and how to use it in detail. Furthermore, we made minor enhancements to our home page visible here: https://githoney.io/ , which gives a high level overview of the product. 

A support channel for end-users to resolve questions and issues

We have set up 2 support channels.
・In the form of a Discord channel on TxPipe’s Discord server. Can be found here: https://discord.gg/ZTHcHUy5HY . Our homepage links to said Discord channel.
・Support email on our home page. 

Added a screenshot below of how one could access our support from the info provided on our landing page https://githoney.io/ . 

Acceptance criteria:

Any end-user is able to run the complete lifecycle of a bounty using the services and information publicly available.

Given the information and steps detailed in the documentation page , as well as on the home page of GitHoney, the user should have all the necessary information to be able to install GitHoney, create a bounty, deposit the reward, accept the bounty and claim the bounty. Promoting GitHoney Among Major Cardano Organizations
TxPipe has been actively advocating for GitHoney as an innovative and transparent bounty management solution across key stakeholders within the Cardano ecosystem. Below is an overview of our outreach efforts and engagements:
Engagement with Project Catalyst
We introduced GitHoney to the Project Catalyst team as a potential tool to enhance transparency and accountability in managing funded projects. A formal email was sent, highlighting GitHoney’s alignment with Catalyst’s goals. We are currently awaiting a formal response. Additionally, we had in-person discussions with Kriss Baird, a Catalyst team member, during the Cardano Summit event in Buenos Aires (November 2024). The project was well-received, and we encouraged its consideration as a valuable tool for Catalyst.
Outreach to IOG (Input Output Global)
We reached out to IOG, emphasizing GitHoney’s potential to drive broader community engagement, particularly among students and developers. A formal proposal was sent to Robertino Martinez, lead of IOG’s education team, outlining how GitHoney can inspire students to contribute to open-source projects while gaining valuable hands-on experience. We met Robertino in Buenos Aires (October 2024) and discussed the project further. The reception was very positive, and we are now awaiting IOG’s formal feedback.
Promotion within PRAGMA
As an active member of PRAGMA, TxPipe has been promoting GitHoney’s adoption within the organization. During the Cardano Summit in Buenos Aires (November 2024), we introduced the project to Kriss Gianelloni, CEO of BlinkLabs and a founding member of PRAGMA, demonstrating GitHoney’s potential to streamline workflows and support collaborative projects.
